phase: route four - can the loader read /data's blocks directly?
result: NO - /data is encrypted at the block layer
question: Android allocates and pins image files inside /data; if the loader could follow the extent map to the physical partition it would get a large block device without any FBE work and without touching the GPT. This trial asked whether that read is plaintext.

evidence.observed: /dev/block/dm-50, f2fs, with inlinecrypt in the mount options
exactly one slave: /dev/block/sdc86, the physical userdata partition (103.98 GiB)
dm-50 has 4073 non-zero bytes, sdc86 is all zeros there

evidence.step: same offset in both, block 0 offset 1024 -- where an f2fs superblock lives
evidence.observed: dm-50 reads 10 20 f5 f2 (the f2fs magic 0xF2F52010, little endian); sdc86 reads random-looking bytes at the same place

conclusion: dm-50 is not a linear mapping of sdc86. The physical partition holds ciphertext: the f2fs superblock is legible through dm-50 and unreadable directly on sdc86. Metadata encryption (AES-256-XTS with a key in the metadata partition) sits at the block layer, under the file system.
what_this_settles: route four is closed as stated: following extents to sdc86 yields ciphertext
no amount of offset or unit correction would fix this -- the bytes themselves differ
what_would_still_be_needed: the metadata encryption key, which lives in the keymaster/keystore chain
or a partition that is not encrypted at all
what_this_rules_out_for_the_gpt_plan: splitting userdata would produce another encrypted-by-default volume unless the new entry is deliberately left unencrypted, and shrinking the file system is the real difficulty anyway
next: measure the var_store archive size, which needs nothing new
or design an unencrypted data area, which means a GPT change and a file system that can shrink
